title: BITS: Bi-level Imitation for Traffic Simulation

control_signal.value: No user-facing control signal stated. Internally, agents are conditioned on a sampled short-horizon goal (target position and heading); a rule-based cost with a set of weights selects among sampled actions.

control_mechanism.value: Spatial goal network outputs a 2D goal likelihood map; goal-conditional policy decodes actions per sampled goal; a prediction-and-planning module picks actions minimizing a rule-following cost on predicted future states.

base_model.value: Hierarchical imitation: ResNet-18 encoder on rasterized map and agent history, U-Net-style spatial goal decoder, MLP trajectory decoder with unicycle dynamics, plus a future-state trajectory predictor.

datasets.value: Lyft Level 5 (1000 hours, Palo Alto) and nuScenes (5.5 hours, Boston and Singapore).

metrics.value: Failure rate, collision rate, offroad rate, coverage, diversity; Wasserstein distance on speed and jerk; sADE; learned occupancy-likelihood score (Lyft 0.131, nuScenes 0.276 for BITS).

controllability_evidence.value: No controllability experiment in packet. Evidence is stability and diversity: BITS reaches high diversity and coverage with low failure rate, and lower failure rates than recorded data on both datasets.

stated_limitations.value: Metrics are only proxies for realism and the learned metric may be biased; traffic rules not evaluated; data-driven models inherit bias from training regions.

notes: Not a controllable-generation paper; included for the goal-conditioning and cost-based action selection. Control family choice is a judgement call.
